description_en: Chusyā Bāhāḥ is one of the oldestbāhāḥsin Kathmandu and one of only threebāhāḥsthat has preserved its original courtyard floor plan. There are debates concerning thebāhāḥ'sinitial construction date. Karel Rijk van Kooij (1977, 39-82) is of the opinion that the iconography and stylistic details of the roof brackets are concurrent with drawings found in eleventh century manuscripts. Shantaram Balchandra Deo (1969, 10-11) dated the struts to the fourteenth century.The earliest sources related to thebāhāḥare two stone inscriptions issued during the reign of King Pratāpa Malla (r. 1641-74): a well-preserved inscription from NS 788 (1668 CE) and a damaged inscription, most probably issued before NS 788 (1668 CE). The physical and palaeographical features of these inscriptions suggest that they were issued by the same person a few years apart.The NS 788 (1668 CE) inscription records the consecration of Guṇākara Mahāvihāra (Chusyā Bāhāḥ) ‘guṇākara mahāvihāra pratiṣṭhā saṃpūrṇa yāṅana’ and the installation of Harāhara Lokeśvara, sponsored by a person named Guṇajyoti (text: Guṇajoti) Vajrācārya together with his family members from Dhvākhā Bāhāḥ, while the damaged inscription mentions the completion of thebāhāḥ‘thva vihara dayakā’.A third inscription also installed by Guṇajyoti inside the sanctum of thebāhāḥin NS 769 (1649 CE) records the renovation of a rest-house (capāḥ) constructed by his father Jñānajyoti (text: Jñānajoti) in honour of their clan deity, Maricī Devī. This indicates that there was a shrine or apīṭha(abode) dedicated to Maricī Devī nearby. Chusyā Bāhāḥ is not mentioned in this inscription. If the expansive Mahāvihāra had existed here during this time, it would have been probably mentioned in the inscription which records the family tree of Guṇajyoti and the renovation of thecapāḥ.Thus, it is likely that the damaged inscription was issued after NS 769 (1649 CE). We can then conclude that thebāhāḥmust have been constructed sometime after NS 769 (1649 CE), and was consecrated (probably after its renovation) in NS 788 (1668 CE). One could also argue that Guṇajyoti converted thecapāḥbuilt by his father into abāhāḥand named it Guṇākara Mahāvihāra (Chusyā Bāhāḥ) after him. Chusyā Bāhāḥ'ssaṅghamembers believe that Guṇajyoti constructed thebāhāḥwith income generated from his trade in Tibet.Locke(1985, 274) writes: “For the history of Chusyā Bāhāḥ we would seem to be on very firm ground, but records are deceptive. There is an inscription at the bāhā dated N.S. 788 which says that the construction of the bāhāḥ was completed in N.S. 769 and at the time an image of Harihara Lokeśvara was installed in the shrine. The donors were Vajracarya Guṇajyoti, his first wife Yadumani Lakṣmī and his second wife Helmani Lakṣmi of Dhvākhā Bāhāḥ. In N.S. 788 the King of Kathmandu, Pratāp Malla was invited by Guṇajyoti to the ceremony marking the official opening of the bāhā. …  It seems clear that the bāhā was renovated in N. S. 769, and the occasion marked by the donation of an image of Harihara Lokeśvara some years later. Pratāp Malla was invited to the consecration ceremony of this image. It is impossible to say whether Chusyā Bāhāḥ had long been a branch of Dhwākā Bāhā and was renovated at this time, or whether it was a separate foundation that had been abandoned by its original inhabitants, fallen into disrepair and then taken over and renovated by the people of Dhwākā Bāhā as a branch of their bāhā.”The epigraphic evidence does not support Locke’s interpretation. First, the NS 788 inscription does not say that the construction of thebāhāḥwas completed in NS 769. As mentioned above, it simply records that the consecration of Guṇākara Mahāvihāra was completed. Second, the inscription does not mention that King Pratāpa Malla was invited by Guṇajyoti to the consecration ceremony of Harāhara[1]Lokeśvara, it merely mentions that the events recorded in the inscription took place in the kingdom ruled (‘lit. concurred,vijayarājye’) by King Pratāpa Malla. It is a common feature to mention the reigning king in the inscriptions.Furthermore, other inscriptions and objects installed in thebāhāḥare dated after Guṇajyoti’s NS 788 inscription. For example, thetoraṇacrowning the main entrance dates from 1673 CE (NS 793),[2]and the one above thekvāḥpāḥdyaḥ’sdoor is from 1676 CE (NS 796).[3]APrajñāpāramitāmanuscript copied in NS 798 (1678 CE) during the reign of King Bhūpatīndra Malla of Bhaktapur is kept in thebāhāḥ, which is recited during the Guṃlā ‘Kārtika’ month (cf.A. Vajrācārya, VS 2071, 31). Parikhadeva, grandson (nāti) of Guṇajyoti, paid the Vajrācāryas (Bidupatideva, Bekhā Siṃha, Jayadharmadeva and Dhanamuni) from Śrīkhaṇdatarumūla Mahāvihāra (Sikhaṃmū Vihāra) for copying the manuscript to be recited in thebāhāḥ.In 1699 CE (NS 819), Parikhadeva installed his own statue, flanked by his two wives, Vidhyādharī and Dhavati, in front of the principal deity of the bāhāḥ (kvāḥpāḥdyaḥ), making himself the Vajrasattva.[4]In the light of these activities, it is clear that Guṇajyoti’s descendants continued to worship in thebāhāḥand expanded it.Akṣobhya was consecrated in the sanctum as thebāhāḥ’sprincipal deity (kvāḥpāḥdyaḥ).There used to be traditional wall-paintings in the sanctum. They were destroyed during a botched maintenance effort two decades ago which was carried out without any archaeological investigation.Between 1996 CE and 2003 CE, thebāhāḥwas restored with technical support from the Kathmandu Valley Preservation Trust and funding provided by the International Union for the Conservation of Nature and the German Foreign Office.In the past, Chusyā Bāhāḥ was used as a school and a workshop. It is one of the very few monasteries that has not been cut-up and privatized.The courtyard building is relatively intact, preserved with all its original doors, windows, and four exceptionally artistic tympanums, two of them bearing dates (CE 1673 and CE 1676). Unfortunately, many of its roof struts have been lost and many of the stone sculptures displayed in the courtyard are severely damaged and have been patched with an unknown material, possibly a cement compound. Historic photographs (Pruscha, ca. 1973, Locke, ca. 1984, Klimek, 2003) reveal a number of changes: the donor figure and his two wives, previously free-standing, received a new enclosure; two small stonecaityasnow flank the donor figures; a historic pillar with a lion was added, and the Lokeśvara statue was moved and enclosed in a small stone shrine. The two main stone inscriptions flanking the door of thekvāpaḥdyaḥcannot be seen in Pruscha's photograph.A miniature stone temple (Mañjuśrīdegaḥ KAT0160-016), which used to stand in front of the main gate, was moved to thebāhāḥ'scourtyard in 1970 CE (NS 1090) during the widening of the road from Jamal to Jyāthā.Chusyā Bāhāḥ'ssaṅghawas comprised of members of the Vajrācārya clans from Dhvākhā Bāhāḥ who used to be responsible to perform the daily rituals. Since many of them have moved away, the responsibility for the daily rituals now rests on others who live nearby.In the present-day, the Vajrācāryas from Dhvākhā Bāhāḥ visit thebāhāḥoccasionally to worship thebāhāḥ’sesoteric deity (āgaṃdyaḥ),which is housed in the upper storey.ThePrajñāpāramitāmanuscript is recited for a week during the month of Guṃlā, an ancient tradition that has been preserved to this day. During this month, valuable objects such as ancient statues that are kept in thebāhāḥare publicly displayed. On the behest of a local social organisation, meditation programmes take place every Saturday.Vajrayāna Mahāvihāra, a monastery in Lumbini, uses the southern wing of thebāhāḥas its Kathmandu office.Footnotes^Locke 1985, 274 and Gutschow (2011, 738) read it as ‘Harihara’.^The image of Prajñāpāramitā, Chepu,dancing ladies to the right and left of the deity etc. are carved on this strut.^Numerous Buddhist deities are intricately carved on it.^Gutschow (2011, vol 2, 738) erroneously mentions that this is a statue of Guṇajyoti and his two wives.
description_ne: काठमाडौंको ज्याथा टोलमा एकै सडकको किनारामा दुई बाहाःहरू अवस्थित छन् –छुस्या बाहाःरमुस्या बाहाः। यी दुईमध्ये मुस्याबाहाःले आफ्नो मौलिक स्वरूप गुमाइसकेको छ भने छुस्या बाहाः उपत्यकामै मौलिक वास्तुसंरचनामा हालसम्म पनि जीवन्त रहन सफल गिनेचुनेका बाहाःमध्येमा पर्दछ ।छुस्या बाहाःको प्रारम्भिक निर्माणको सन्दर्भमा अन्यौलता पाइन्छ । केही विद्वानहरूमा बाहाःमा भएका टुँडालहरू १४–१५ औं शताव्दीका हुन् भन्ने धारणा छ[1]तर बाहाःमा प्राप्त प्रतापमल्लकालीन एक (मिति खिइसकेको)  अभिलेखमा‘थ्व विहार दयका’(यो विहार बनाइयो) भनिएको छ ।‘विहार बनाइयो’भन्ने वाक्यांशले पहिलेनै अस्तित्वमा भएको विहारलाई पुनः निर्माण गरिएको नभई प्रारम्भिक निर्माणलाई नै जनाउन खोजेको देखिन्छ । यहाँ भएको अर्को प्रतापमल्लकालीन सन् (नेसं ७८८) को अभिलेखमा गुणज्योति बज्राचार्यले‘गुणाकर महाविहार प्रतिष्ठा संपूर्ण याङन’ (महाविहार स्थापनाकार्य पूर्ण गरी.....)भनिएको छ । यी दुई अभिलेखलाई नियाल्दा तिथिमिति खिइसकेको तर प्रतापमल्लको प्रशस्ति परेको अभिलेखमा विहार निर्माण कार्य प्रारम्भ गरिएको र निर्माण कार्य सम्पन्न भए पश्चात् सन् (नेसं ७८८) को अभिलेख राखिएको बोध हुन्छ । गुणज्योतिले प्रारम्भिक निर्माण गरेकै कारण उनकै नमबाट यसको संस्कृत नाम‘गुणाकार महाविहार’ राखिएको प्रतीत हुन्छ । विहार निर्माणकार्य सम्पन्न भएकै अवसरमा ध्वाखा बाहाःका उनै गुणज्योतिले बाहाः आसपास कतै फल्चा जीर्णोद्धार गरी हलाहल लोकेश्वरको प्रतिमा पनि स्थापना गरेको कुरा साेही अभिलेखमा उद्धृत गरिएको छ ।[2]बाहाःमा भएका टुँडालहरू १४–१५ औं शताव्दीका हुन् भन्ने केही विद्वानहरूको मान्यतालाई टेकीLocke(1985, 274) ले विगतमा सम्बन्धित संघबाट त्यागिएको जीर्ण बाहाःलाई उक्त मितिमा ढोका बाहाःका गुणज्योतिले पुनःनिर्माण गरी ध्वाखा बाहाःकै शाखा विहारका रूपमा यस बाहाःलाई आवद्ध गरेको पनि हुन सक्ने कुरा औंलाएका छन् । बाहाःको गर्भगृहभित्र ठड्याइएको एक अभिलेखमा सन् (नेसं ७६९) मा ध्वाखा बाहाःका ज्ञानज्योति बज्राचार्यले आफ्ना इष्टदेवीमरिची देवीको नाममा चपाः निर्माण गरेको उल्लेख छ । यसबाट उक्त मितिमा हाल बाहाः भएको ठाउँ वरपर कतै मरिची देवीको पीठ वा  shrine भएको कुरा ज्ञात हुन्छ । यो अलिभेखमा छुस्याबाहाःको कतैपनि नामोल्लेख छैन । यहाँ चपाः बनाउने ज्ञानज्योतिका छोराका रूपमा गुणज्योतिको नाम उल्लेख छ ।ज्ञानज्योतिकै पालामा यस स्थानमा महाविहार स्वरूपको भव्य संरचना अस्तित्वमा भएको भए बनाइएको चपाःको अवस्थिति औंल्याउँदा उक्त चपाः समीपैको विहारको पनि पक्कै नामोल्लेख अभिलेखमा हुने थियो । आफ्नो कुलको इष्टदेवीको नामका आफ्ना बुबाले चपाः बनाएकै ठाउँमा छोरा गुणज्योतिले पनि कीर्ति थपी गुणाकर महाविहारको प्रारम्भिक निर्माण गरेको देखिन्छ । गुणज्योति बज्राचार्यले तिब्बतबाट कमाएको मनग्गे धनबाट यो विहार निर्माण गरेको हो भन्ने बलियो परम्परागत विश्वास छुस्या बाहाः संघका सदस्यहरूमा यद्यपि पाइनु पनि सोचनीय छ ।  गुणज्योतिले राखेको माथि उल्लेखित सन् (नेसं ७८८) को अलिभेख पछि मात्र बाहाःमा तोरण लगायत अन्य वस्तुहरू थपिँदै लगिएका अन्य अभिलेखहरू प्राप्त छन् ।बाहाःमा वर्षेनी गुंला महिनामा पाठ गरिने प्रज्ञापारमिता ग्रन्थ छ । उक्त ग्रन्थको पुष्पिका वाक्यमा गुणज्योतिका नाति परिखदेवले सन् (नेसं ७९८) मा श्रीखण्ड तरुमुल महाविहार (सिखंमू बाहाः) का बज्राचार्यहरू बिदुपति देव, बेखासिंह, जयधर्म देव, धनमुनि देव आदिको हस्तलेखनबाट उक्त ग्रन्थ तयार गराएको कुरा उल्लेख छ । साथै यस ग्रन्थलेखनकार्य समापनको उपलक्ष्यमा भक्तपुरका राजा भूपतिन्द्र मल्ल पनि उपस्थित भएको कुरा पुष्पिकावाक्यमा लेखिएको छ (A. Vajrācārya, VS 2071, 31) । उनै परिखदेवले सन् (नेसं ८१९) मा क्वाःपाःद्यःको अगाडि आफ्नो नाममा बज्रसत्व र दायाँ–बायाँ विद्याधरि (परिखदेवकी पत्नी) र धओतिको प्रतिमा स्थापना गरेका थिए ।[3]यी तथ्यले यो विहारप्रति गुणज्यातिको वंशको उल्लेख्य आस्था रहेको र क्रमिक रूपमा सोही वंशबाट कीर्ति थप्ने कार्य हुँदै गएको कुरा ज्ञात हुन्छ ।काष्ठकलाका दृष्टिले पनि यो बाहाः निकै उल्लेखनीय छ । क्वापाःछेँको छानो थमाइएका टुँडालहरूमा बौद्ध तन्त्रमा आधारित निकै नै कलात्मक मूर्तिहरूको चित्रण देख्न सकिन्छ । ती टुँडालका साथै चौतर्फी भएका टुँडालहरूको तल्लो भागमा तत्–तत् टुँडालमा चित्रित देवदेवीको नामोल्लेख पनि परेका छन् जसबाट तिनको पहिचानमा ठुलो सहायता मिलेको छ ।  बाहाःको मूलढोका माथिको तोरण सन् १६७३ (नेसं ७९३) को हो । यसमा भएको छेपुको रूप, केन्द्रमा भएका प्रज्ञापारमिताको दायाँ–बायाँ कुँदिएका नृत्यमग्न नारीमूर्ति र ड्रेगनको उपस्थिति आदिलाई मध्यकालीन अन्य तोरणमा नपाइँने पृथक विशेषता मान्न सकिन्छ । क्वाःपाःद्यःको ढोकामाथि राखिएको सन् १६७६ (नेसं ७९६) को तोरण पनि उपत्यकाका उल्लेखनीय तोरणहरूमध्येमा पर्दछ । यस तोरणको मध्य भागमा धर्मधातुवागीश्वर र अन्य बौद्ध मूर्तिहरूको कलात्मक प्रस्तुति देख्न सकिन्छ ।क्वाःपाःद्यःको रूपमा यहाँ अक्ष्योभ्यको शिलामूर्ति स्थापित छ । क्वाःपाःद्यः स्थापित गर्भगृहमा विगत भित्तेचित्रहरू पनि कोरिएका थिए । पुरातात्विक ज्ञान बिनै गरिएको मर्मत कार्यका नाममा ती ऐतिहासिक भित्तेचित्रहरू करिब दुई दशक अघि नष्ट भए । जमलबाट ज्याथा टोलमा गाडी प्रवेश गर्न सम्भव हुने गरी सन् १९७०  (नेसं १०९०) मा मोटरबाटो निर्माण हुँदा बाहाःको मूलढोका अगाडि भएको मञ्जुश्रीदेगः (KAT0160-016) लाई बाहाःभित्र स्थानान्तरण गरिएको थिाये । सन् १९९९ सम्म बाहाःको भवन र चोक एक प्राथमिक विद्यालयको रूपमा प्रयोजनमा थियो । विद्याःलयले बाहाः छाडे पश्तात् International Union for the Conservation of Nature (IUCN) र German Foreign Ministry  को सहकार्य लगायत KVPT बाट यहाँ विभिन्न चरणमा मर्मतकार्यहरू भएका छन् ।यो बाहाः ध्वाखा बाहाः अन्तर्गतको कचा बाहाःहरूमध्येको एक हो । ध्वाखा बाहाःअन्तर्गतका बज्राचार्य खलकहरू यस बाहाःमा संघ सदस्यका रूपमा छन् ।[4]विगत एक दशक अगाडि संघका बज्राचार्य सदस्यहरूले प्रत्येक महिनाको अन्तरालमा छुस्या बाहाःमा नित्य पूजाको अभिभारा वहन गर्दै आएका थिए । प्राय सदस्यहरू ध्वाखा बाहाः परिसर छोडी अन्यत्र बसाई सरे पश्चात् यसै बाहाःको दक्षिणमा घर भएका संघ सदस्यले दशकौं देखि नित्य पूजा संचालन गर्दै आएका छन् । जन्मदिन, शुभ साइत तथा पुण्य तिथिहरूमा भने संघका अन्य सदस्यहरू द्यःछेँको माथिल्लो तल्लामा स्थापित आगंद्यःलाई पूज्न आउने कार्य भने यद्यपि कायम छ । बाहाःमा गुणज्योतिका नाति परिखदेवको पालामा अर्थात् सन् १६७८ (नेसं ७९८) मा लिखित प्रज्ञापारमिता ग्रन्थ छ । उक्त ग्रन्थ गुंला महिनाको एक साता पाठ गर्ने परम्परा हालसम्म पनि चली आएको छ । सोही महिनामा बाहाःको पश्चिमी खण्डमा बहीद्यः ब्वय्‌गु अर्थात् बाहाःको संग्रहमा रहेका विविध ऐतिहासिक मूर्ति एवं अन्य मूल्यवान् वस्तु प्रदर्शनमा राख्ने परम्परा पनि चल्दै आएको छ । परम्परागत बौद्ध धर्म संघ, काठमाडौं शाखाको अगुवाइमा बाहाःभित्र प्रत्येक शनिवार ध्यान कार्यक्रम पनि हुने गरेको छ । बाहाःको पश्चिमी खण्ड हाल लुम्बिनीमा निर्माणाधीन बज्रयान महाविहारको सम्पर्क कार्यलयको रूपमा प्रयोजनमा छ । अस्त–व्यस्त काठमाडौं नगरभित्रको खुल्ला तथा शान्त वातावरण भएको ठाउँ भएबाट यस बाहाः परिसरभित्र बेलाबखत सामाजिक एवं सांस्कृतिक कार्यक्रमहरू पनि संचालन हुने गरेका छन् ।Footnotes^Karel Rijk van Kooij(1977, 39-82)  का अनुसार यहाँका टुँडालहरूमा चित्रित मूर्तिहरूको प्रतिमालक्षण ११ औं शदीका निष्पन्नयोगावली, साधनमाला, धारणीसंग्रह जस्ता हस्तलिखित ग्रन्थहरूबाट प्रेरित देखिन्छन् ।Shantaram Balchandra Deo(1969, 10-11) ले यी टुँडाललाई १४ औं शताब्दीको क्रममा हालेका छन् ।^Locke(1985, 274) रGutschow(2011, vol - 1, 33)  दुबैले हलाहल लोकेश्वरको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको उपलक्ष्यमा तत्कालीन राजा प्रताप मल्ल पनि विहारमा आमन्त्रित थिए भनी लेखेका छन्, तर उक्त अलिभेखमा विहार परिसरमा कतै चर्किएर रहेको फल्चा मर्मत गरी लोकेश्वरको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएकोे मात्र प्रसंग छ । अभिलेखको शिरोभागमा प्रशस्ति स्वरूप ‘राजा प्रतापमल्लको शासनकालमा’ मात्र भनिएका छ, राजाको आमन्त्रणको कुनै उल्लेखन परेको देखिँदैन ।^Gutschow(2011, vol - 2, 738) ले गल्तीवस् यी प्रतिमालाई गुणज्योति र उनकी दुई पत्नीको भनी भनेका छन् ।^Gutschow(2011, vol - 2, 738) ले गल्तीवस् यस बाहाःमा शाक्य समुदायका ३२ सदस्यीय संघ रहेको कुरा लेखेका छन्।

historical_events.event_description: From 1996 CE to 2003 CE, the roofs were replaced with the financial support of the International Union for the Conservation of Nature (IUCN) and the German Foreign Ministry. The Kathmandu Valley Preservataion Trust (KVPT) provided technical support.
The miniature stone temple of Mañjuśrī was moved from the north of the Bāhāḥto the courtyard.

historical_events.event_name: Use as a School and Workshops
historical_events.event_description: Until 1999 CE, the arcaded ground floors were used by a school, while other rooms were inappropriately used as workshops.

In 2008 CE, the stone objects that were kept in the courtyard were rearranged on new pedestals. The statues of Parikhadeva and his two wives were placed on a new base and protected under a masonry arch. Tīrthadhara Tulādhara of Jana Bāhāḥ, Kathmandu, sponsored all the necessary expenses for this intervention.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of a Glass Case in the Sanctum
historical_events.event_description: In 2009 CE, thekvāḥpāḥdyaḥ(principal deity) was painted and enshrined in a glass case.
In 2016 CE, the glass case of the principal deity was removed as it had attracted rats to nest in it.

historical_events.event_name: The Initial Construction of the Bāhāḥ
historical_events.event_description: The inscription (date unreadable) issued during the reign of King Pratāpa Malla (r. 1641-1674 CE) mentions that ‘this Vihāra is constructed’ (thva vihara dayakā). It most likely refers to the initial construction of Chusyā Bāhāḥ.

historical_events.event_name: Consecration of the Bāhāḥ, Renovation of the Capāḥ, and Installation of Harāhara Lokeśvara
historical_events.event_description: The inscription records that the consecration of Guṇākara Mahāvihāra sponsored by Guṇajyoti is completed. It further mentions the renovation of thephalcāsomewhere near the Bāhāḥ and installation of the statue of Harāhara Lokeśvara there.
Pramānananda and his family members installed a bell in front of thedyaḥchẽ.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of the Statue of Parikhadeva
historical_events.event_description: The inscription records that Parikhadeva installed his own statue, flanked by his two wives Vidhyādhari and Dhavati, representing him in the form of a Vajrasattva.
In the name of Saṅgharatna and his family members, the stone statue of Padmapāṇi Lokeśvara was established in the courtyard.
Gutschow (2011, vol 2, 738), without referring to any source, mentions '...the present guarding deity Akṣobhya [, which] was donated in 1715 CE by King Bhūpatīndramalla of Bhaktapur.'
A piece of silver jewellery was offered to thekvāḥpāḥdyaḥby Sumana Vajrācārya of Māhābauddha, Kathmandu, in the name of late Yāviratna Vajrācārya,

historical_events.event_name: Addition of a Toraṇa over the Main Entrance
historical_events.event_description: A woodentoraṇa,featuring Prajñāpāramitā at the centre, was installed over the main entrance from the north.

historical_events.event_name: Completion of the Copying of a Prajñāpāramitā Manuscript
historical_events.event_description: The Prajñāpāramitā manuscript, which is recited during the Guṃlā (Kārtika), is kept in the Bāhāḥ. Its colophon mentions that Parikhadeva, Guṇajyoti’s grandson, sponsored for the copying of this manuscript.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of a Capāḥ (a roofed resting place)
historical_events.event_description: The inscription records the construction of acapāḥnear Chusyā Bāhāḥ by Jñānajoti and family members in the name of Maricī Devī. Jñānajoti was from Dhvākhā Bāhāḥ and the father of Guṇajyoti, the founder of Chusyā Bāhāḥ.

historical_events.event_name: Offerings of a Toraṇa and a Gilt Parasol
historical_events.event_description: A group of Vajrācāryas and Śākyas from differentbāhāsoffered a gilt parasol to thekvāḥpāḥdyaḥ. At the same time, a woodentoraṇawas mounted over the entrance of the main shrine.
Since the middle part of the inscription is damaged, the events recorded remain obscure.
